fr.L: Et Corneille dit : « Depuis le quatrième jour jusqu’à cette heure-ci, je priais la neuvième [heure] dans ma maison, et voici qu’un homme s’est tenu devant moi en vêtement éclatant \v 31 et il dit : “Corneille, ta prière a été entendue et tes aumônes ont été rappelées devant Dieu.
fr.B: Corneille répondit : « Il y a quatre jours, à cette heure-ci, à quinze heures, j’étais chez moi en prière. Soudain, un homme aux vêtements resplendissants s’est tenu devant moi. \v 31 Il m’a dit : “Corneille, Dieu a entendu ta prière et s’est souvenu de tes dons aux pauvres.
fr.R: Corneille a dit : « Il y a quatre jours, à la même heure, à trois heures de l’après-midi, je priais dans ma maison. Tout à coup, un homme aux vêtements brillants était là, devant moi. \v 31 Il m’a dit : “Corneille, Dieu a entendu ta prière. Il a vu ce que tu donnes aux pauvres, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en souvient.

sw.L: Naye Kornelio akasema, "Siku nne zilizopita, mpaka saa hii, nilikuwa nikiomba [sala ya] saa tisa nyumbani mwangu, na tazama, mtu mmoja akasimama mbele yangu akiwa amevaa mavazi yanayong'aa, \v 31 naye anasema, 'Kornelio, maombi yako yamesikiwa, na sadaka zako zimekumbukwa mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Kornelio akajibu, "Siku nne zilizopita, saa kama hii, saa tisa mchana, nilikuwa nyumbani mwangu nikiomba. Ghafla mtu mmoja aliyevaa mavazi yanayong'aa alisimama mbele yangu. \v 31 Akasema, 'Kornelio, Mungu amesikia maombi yako, na amekumbuka misaada yako kwa maskini.
sw.R: Kornelio akasema, "Siku nne zilizopita, wakati kama huu, saa tisa mchana, nilikuwa nikiomba nyumbani mwangu. Ghafla mtu mmoja aliyevaa nguo zinazong'aa sana alikuwa amesimama mbele yangu. \v 31 Akasema, 'Kornelio, Mungu amesikia maombi yako. Ameona misaada unayowapa maskini, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anaikumbuka.

decisions.choice: from the fourth day until this hour: four days ago, at this same time of day
alternatives: he prayed without stopping for four days
decisions.reason: The phrase counts back to the same hour four days before, counting both the first and the last day (10:3, 10:9, 10:23-24). The Greek is compressed, and "the ninth" names the hour of prayer, as in 10:3.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "praying"
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "fasting and praying"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "I was fasting, and at the ninth hour I was praying". The early manuscripts do not have "fasting". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man in bright clothing: the angel of 10:3, appearing as a man
decisions.reason: Angels appear as men in shining clothes in Luke 24:4 and Acts 1:10. Luke has already called him an angel (10:3).

decisions.choice: has been heard ... remembered before God: God has heard and taken notice
alternatives: God has rewarded his good works
decisions.reason: The passive verbs mean that God has done this, as 10:4 says.

decisions.choice: God has heard ... has remembered
alternatives: has been heard ... have been remembered before God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who acts, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the passives.

decisions.choice: three in the afternoon
decisions.reason: As at 10:3.

source.text: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος· οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ θάλασσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Send therefore to Joppa and call for Simon who is called Peter; this one lodges in [the] house of Simon a tanner by [the] sea.

en.L: So send to Joppa and call for Simon, who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by [the] sea.'
en.B: So send to Joppa and ask Simon, who is called Peter, to come. He is staying as a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.'
en.R: Send some men to Joppa to bring back Simon, who is also called Peter. He is staying in the house of a man named Simon, who makes leather. His house is near the sea.'

es.L: Envía, pues, a Jope y haz llamar a Simón, que es llamado Pedro; este se hospeda en casa de Simón, curtidor, junto al mar”.
es.B: Así que envía a alguien a Jope y pide a Simón, al que llaman Pedro, que venga. Está alojado en casa de Simón el curtidor, junto al mar”.
es.R: Envía a unos hombres a Jope para que traigan a Simón, al que también llaman Pedro. Se está quedando en la casa de un hombre llamado Simón, que trabaja el cuero. Su casa está cerca del mar”.

fr.L: Envoie donc à Joppé et fais appeler Simon, qui est surnommé Pierre ; il loge dans la maison de Simon, un tanneur, près de [la] mer.”
fr.B: Envoie donc quelqu’un à Joppé et fais venir Simon, qu’on appelle Pierre. Il est l’hôte de Simon le tanneur, au bord de la mer.”
fr.R: Envoie des hommes à Joppé pour ramener Simon, qu’on appelle aussi Pierre. Il habite chez un homme qui s’appelle Simon et qui fabrique du cuir. Sa maison est près de la mer.”

sw.L: Basi tuma [watu] Yafa, umwite Simoni anayeitwa Petro; yeye anakaa kama mgeni katika nyumba ya Simoni, fundi wa ngozi, kando ya bahari.'
sw.B: Basi tuma watu Yafa, umwombe Simoni anayeitwa Petro aje. Yeye ni mgeni nyumbani mwa Simoni fundi wa ngozi, kando ya bahari.'
sw.R: Tuma watu Yafa wamlete Simoni, anayeitwa pia Petro. Anakaa nyumbani kwa mtu aitwaye Simoni, anayetengeneza ngozi za wanyama. Nyumba yake iko karibu na bahari.'

decisions.choice: SBLGNT ends the angel's words here
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "he will speak to you when he comes"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "who, when he comes, will speak to you". The early manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: who makes leather
decisions.reason: As at 10:6.

source.text: ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: At once therefore I sent to you, you and well did having come.

en.L: So I sent to you at once, and you have done well to come.
en.B: I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come.
en.R: So I sent for you right away. Thank you for coming.

es.L: Así que al instante envié por ti, y tú hiciste bien en venir.
es.B: Mandé a buscarte enseguida, y has sido muy amable en venir.
es.R: Por eso mandé a buscarte enseguida. Gracias por venir.

fr.L: Aussitôt donc j’ai envoyé [quelqu’un] vers toi, et toi, tu as bien fait de venir.
fr.B: Je t’ai aussitôt fait appeler, et tu as eu la bonté de venir.
fr.R: Alors je t’ai fait appeler tout de suite. Merci d’être venu.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mara moja nilituma [watu] kwako, nawe umefanya vema kuja.
sw.B: Nilituma watu kukuita mara moja, nawe umefanya vizuri kuja.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nilituma watu kukuita mara moja. Asante kwa kuja.

decisions.choice: you have done well to come: a polite word of thanks
alternatives: a judgment that Peter obeyed God
decisions.reason: The phrase is a common courtesy, meaning "thank you for coming", as in 3 John 6.

decisions.choice: Thank you for coming
alternatives: you have done well to come
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the courtesy.

source.text: νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: Now therefore all we before the God are present to hear all the things having been commanded you by the Lord.

en.L: So now we are all here in the presence of God to hear all the things that have been commanded you by the Lord."
en.B: Now we are all here before God, ready to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to say."
en.R: Now we are all here, and God is here with us. We want to hear everything the Lord has told you to say to us."

es.L: Ahora, pues, todos nosotros estamos aquí delante de Dios para oír todo lo que te ha sido ordenado por el Señor».
es.B: Ahora estamos todos aquí, delante de Dios, dispuestos a escuchar todo lo que el Señor te ha mandado decir».
es.R: Ahora estamos todos aquí, y Dios está aquí con nosotros. Queremos oír todo lo que el Señor te ha dicho que nos digas».

fr.L: Maintenant donc, nous sommes tous présents devant Dieu pour entendre tout ce qui t’a été ordonné par le Seigneur. »
fr.B: Nous voici donc tous devant Dieu, prêts à écouter tout ce que le Seigneur t’a chargé de nous dire. »
fr.R: Maintenant, nous sommes tous ici, et Dieu est là avec nous. Nous voulons entendre tout ce que le Seigneur t’a dit de nous dire. »

sw.L: Basi sasa sisi sote tupo hapa mbele za Mungu, ili kusikia mambo yote uliyoamriwa na Bwana."
sw.B: Sasa sote tuko hapa mbele za Mungu, tayari kusikiliza kila kitu ambacho Bwana amekuagiza useme."
sw.R: Sasa sote tuko hapa, na Mungu yuko pamoja nasi. Tunataka kusikia kila kitu ambacho Bwana amekuambia utuambie."

decisions.choice: before God: in God's presence, aware that he is listening
decisions.reason: Cornelius knows that God has sent Peter. The gathering listens as people standing before God.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: Cornelius knows God, who sent the angel, but has not yet heard of Jesus as Lord (10:36).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "by the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "by God". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God is here with us
decisions.reason: Readable explains "before God" as being in God's presence.

source.text: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπ’ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having opened then Peter the mouth said, Of truth I perceive that not is a receiver of faces the God, \v 35 but in every nation the [one] fearing him and working righteousness acceptable to him is.

en.L: Then Peter opened [his] mouth and said, "In truth I perceive that God is not one who shows partiality, \v 35 but in every nation the one who fears {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and does righteousness is acceptable to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then Peter began to speak: "In truth I now see that God does not favor one person over another. \v 35 Instead, in every nation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accepts those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and practice righteousness.
en.R: Then Peter began to speak. He said, "This is the truth: I now understand that God treats all people the same. \v 35 He accepts people from every nation who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and live righteous lives.

es.L: Entonces Pedro abrió [su] boca y dijo: «De veras entiendo que Dios no es parcial, \v 35 sino que en toda nación el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} teme y practica la justicia es aceptable para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Entonces Pedro tomó la palabra: «Ahora veo de veras que Dios no favorece a unos más que a otros, \v 35 sino que en toda nación acepta a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} temen y practican la justicia.
es.R: Entonces Pedro empezó a hablar. Dijo: «Esto es verdad: ahora entiendo que Dios trata igual a todas las personas. \v 35 Él acepta a la gente de cualquier nación que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} teme y lleva una vida justa.

fr.L: Alors Pierre, ouvrant la bouche, dit : « En vérité, je comprends que Dieu ne fait pas acception de personnes, \v 35 mais qu’en toute nation celui qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craint et pratique la justice {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} est agréable.
fr.B: Alors Pierre prit la parole : « Je comprends maintenant, en vérité, que Dieu ne favorise personne. \v 35 Au contraire, dans toute nation, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accueille ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craignent et pratiquent la justice.
fr.R: Alors Pierre a commencé à parler. Il a dit : « Voici la vérité : je comprends maintenant que Dieu traite tout le monde de la même façon. \v 35 Il accueille les gens de toutes les nations qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craignent et qui vivent d’une manière juste.

sw.L: Ndipo Petro akafumbua kinywa, akasema, "Kwa kweli natambua kwamba Mungu si mtu wa kupendelea watu, \v 35 bali katika kila taifa mtu anayemcha na kutenda haki anakubalika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Ndipo Petro akaanza kusema: "Kweli sasa naona kwamba Mungu hampendelei mtu mmoja kuliko mwingine. \v 35 Badala yake, katika kila taifa huwakubali wale wanaomcha na kutenda haki.
sw.R: Ndipo Petro akaanza kusema. Alisema, "Huu ndio ukweli: sasa naelewa kwamba Mungu huwatendea watu wote sawa. \v 35 Huwakubali watu kutoka kila taifa wanaomcha na kuishi maisha ya haki.

decisions.choice: one who shows partiality: literally a receiver of faces, one who favors people for who they are outwardly
alternatives: one who judges unfairly in a court only
decisions.reason: The Greek word is built from a Hebrew idiom, to "lift up the face" of someone, meaning to show them favor (Leviticus 19:15, Deuteronomy 10:17). Paul says the same of God in Romans 2:11. God does not favor Jews over Gentiles because of their birth.

decisions.choice: opened his mouth: began to speak at length and solemnly
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a weighty speech, as in 8:35 and Matthew 5:2.

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, it is really so
alternatives: a statement about the truth of the gospel
decisions.reason: The phrase means "indeed", as in 4:27. Peter has come to see it through the vision and Cornelius's story.

decisions.choice: acceptable to him: welcome to God, whatever their nation
alternatives: already saved by their good works
decisions.reason: Peter does not say that Cornelius is saved without hearing the message: the angel sent for Peter so that Cornelius would hear words by which he would be saved (11:14), and Peter goes on to speak of forgiveness through believing in Jesus (10:43). He says that a person's nation is no barrier to God.

decisions.choice: does righteousness: does what is right in God's sight
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a way of life, as Cornelius's prayers and gifts show (10:2).

decisions.choice: does not favor one person over another / treats all people the same
alternatives: is not a receiver of faces
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal uses the standard English phrase for it.

decisions.choice: live righteous lives
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word "righteous" in a natural phrase.

decisions.choice: no es parcial (L); no favorece a unos más que a otros (B); trata igual a todas las personas (R)
decisions.reason: The traditional phrase is opaque to most readers today; these say the same thing plainly (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: ne fait pas acception de personnes (L); ne favorise personne (B); traite tout le monde de la même façon (R)
decisions.reason: "Faire acception de personnes" is the established French phrase for the Greek idiom of receiving faces (m1) and is still understood in careful French, so Literal uses it as the English Literal uses "shows partiality"; Balanced and Readable give the sense in everyday words.

decisions.choice: si mtu wa kupendelea watu (L); hampendelei mtu mmoja kuliko mwingine (B); huwatendea watu wote sawa (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide verb for showing favoritism is "kupendelea" (meaning decision on one who shows partiality); Readable says it positively, as the English Readable does.

source.text: τὸν λόγον ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: The word which he sent to the sons of Israel proclaiming good news of peace through Jesus Christ, this one is of all Lord,

en.L: The word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent to the sons of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (this one is Lord of all),
en.B: This is the message {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent to the people of Israel, bringing the good news that peace has come through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and Jesus is Lord of all.
en.R: This is the message God sent to the people of Israel. It is the good news of peace that comes through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Jesus is Lord over all people.

es.L: La palabra que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envió a los hijos de Israel, anunciando la buena noticia de la paz por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} (este es Señor de todos),
es.B: Este es el mensaje que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} envió al pueblo de Israel, con la buena noticia de que la paz ha venido por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, y Jesús es Señor de todos.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que Dios envió al pueblo de Israel. Es la buena noticia de la paz que viene por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Jesús es Señor de todas las personas.

fr.L: La parole qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyée aux fils d’Israël, en annonçant la bonne nouvelle de la paix par Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (celui-ci est Seigneur de tous),
fr.B: C’est le message qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a envoyé au peuple d’Israël en annonçant la bonne nouvelle : la paix est venue par Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, et Jésus est le Seigneur de tous.
fr.R: C’est le message que Dieu a envoyé au peuple d’Israël. C’est la bonne nouvelle de la paix qui vient par Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Jésus est le Seigneur de tous les gens.

sw.L: Neno ambalo alilituma kwa wana wa Israeli, akihubiri habari njema ya amani kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} (huyu ndiye Bwana wa wote),
sw.B: Huu ndio ujumbe aliowatumia watu wa Israeli, akiwaletea habari njema kwamba amani imekuja kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, naye Yesu ni Bwana wa wote.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao Mungu aliwatumia watu wa Israeli. Ni habari njema ya amani inayokuja kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Yesu ni Bwana wa watu wote.

decisions.choice: the word that he sent: the opening of a sentence Peter does not finish; it points to what his hearers know (10:37)
alternatives: a separate sentence: "he sent the word"
decisions.reason: The phrase stands without a verb of its own. It is most easily read with "you know" in 10:37, as the first of the things Peter's hearers know. Peter's Greek is broken here, as in a speech that pours out.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the word which he sent"
alternatives: several early manuscripts lack "which": "he sent the word to the sons of Israel"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts do not have the relative pronoun, which makes the verse a simple sentence: God sent the word to Israel. Other early manuscripts and most later ones have it, and the SBLGNT prints it. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he sent his word ... good news of peace: the words of Psalm 107:20 and Isaiah 52:7
decisions.reason: In the Greek of Psalm 107:20 God "sent his word and healed them", and Isaiah 52:7 speaks of the feet of one who brings good news of peace. The one who sent is God.

decisions.choice: peace through Jesus Christ: peace with God, which also makes peace between peoples
decisions.reason: The message brings reconciliation with God; here, in a Gentile house, it also brings Jews and Gentiles together (Ephesians 2:17, which also echoes Isaiah 52:7).

decisions.choice: this one is Lord of all: Jesus is Lord of all people, Gentiles as well as Jews
decisions.reason: The word "all" could be people or things. In this setting, where God shows no partiality between nations, it means Lord of Jews and Gentiles alike, as Romans 10:12 says.

decisions.choice: This is the message
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Peter's unfinished phrase a full sentence; the meaning note explains the Greek.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who sent the message.

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish writes "Jesucristo" as one word, so the span takes in the whole name, with "Jesús, el Mesías" as the alternative. The same in 10:48.

source.text: ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης, Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: you know the having happened thing throughout all the Judea, having begun from the Galilee after the baptism which proclaimed John, \v 38 Jesus the from Nazareth, how anointed him the God with Spirit Holy and with power, who went about doing good and healing all those being oppressed by the devil, because the God was with him.

en.L: you yourselves know the thing that happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed: \v 38 Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with [the] Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: You yourselves know the events that took place across all Judea. They began in Galilee, after the baptism John proclaimed. \v 38 They concern Jesus from Nazareth: God anointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the Holy Spirit and with power, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} traveled from place to place doing good and healing everyone the devil held in his grip, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: You know about the things that happened in all the land of the Jews. They started in Galilee, after John told people to be baptized. \v 38 You know about Jesus from Nazareth. God poured out the Holy Spirit and power on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Anointed One. Jesus went everywhere doing good things. He healed all the people whom the devil was hurting and controlling, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:ustedes mismos saben|vosotros mismos sabéis}} lo que sucedió por toda Judea, comenzando desde Galilea después del bautismo que Juan proclamó: \v 38 a Jesús de Nazaret, cómo Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ungió con [el] Espíritu Santo y con poder, quien pasó [por todas partes] haciendo el bien y sanando a todos los dominados por el diablo, porque Dios estaba con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} lo que ocurrió en toda Judea. Comenzó en Galilea, después del bautismo que Juan predicó. \v 38 Se trata de Jesús de Nazaret: Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ungió con el Espíritu Santo y con poder, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fue de un lugar a otro haciendo el bien y sanando a todos los que estaban bajo el dominio del diablo, porque Dios estaba con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} lo que pasó en toda la tierra de los judíos. Todo comenzó en Galilea, después de que Juan le dijo a la gente que se bautizara. \v 38 {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} acerca de Jesús de Nazaret. Dios derramó sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el Espíritu Santo y poder, y así {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hizo el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Ungido. Jesús fue por todas partes haciendo cosas buenas. Sanó a todas las personas a quienes el diablo hacía daño y dominaba, porque Dios estaba con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: vous, vous savez ce qui est arrivé dans toute la Judée, en commençant par la Galilée, après le baptême que Jean a proclamé : \v 38 Jésus de Nazareth, comment Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a oint d’Esprit Saint et de puissance, qui a passé de lieu en lieu en faisant le bien et en guérissant tous ceux qui étaient opprimés par le diable, car Dieu était avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Vous savez vous-mêmes les événements qui se sont produits dans toute la Judée. Ils ont commencé en Galilée, après le baptême que Jean a proclamé. \v 38 Ils concernent Jésus de Nazareth : Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a oint d’Esprit Saint et de puissance, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé de lieu en lieu en faisant le bien et en guérissant tous ceux que le diable tenait sous son emprise, car Dieu était avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Vous savez ce qui s’est passé dans tout le pays des Juifs. Tout a commencé en Galilée, après que Jean a appelé les gens à se faire baptiser. \v 38 Vous connaissez Jésus de Nazareth. Dieu a répandu sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} l’Esprit Saint et la puissance, et c’est ainsi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, celui qui a reçu l’onction. Jésus est allé partout en faisant le bien. Il a guéri tous les gens que le diable faisait souffrir et tenait sous son pouvoir, car Dieu était avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: ninyi wenyewe mnajua jambo lililotokea katika Uyahudi wote, likianzia Galilaya baada ya ubatizo aliouhubiri Yohana: \v 38 Yesu wa Nazareti, jinsi Mungu alivyomtia mafuta kwa Roho Mtakatifu na kwa nguvu, ambaye alizunguka akitenda mema na kuwaponya wote walioonewa na Ibilisi, kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Ninyi wenyewe mnajua mambo yaliyotukia katika Uyahudi wote. Yalianzia Galilaya, baada ya ubatizo aliouhubiri Yohana. \v 38 Yanamhusu Yesu wa Nazareti: Mungu alimtia mafuta kwa Roho Mtakatifu na kwa nguvu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alizunguka kila mahali akitenda mema na kuwaponya wote waliokuwa chini ya nguvu za Ibilisi, kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Mnajua mambo yaliyotokea katika nchi yote ya Wayahudi. Yalianzia Galilaya, baada ya Yohana kuwaambia watu wabatizwe. \v 38 Mnajua habari za Yesu wa Nazareti. Mungu alimmiminia Roho Mtakatifu na nguvu, na hivyo akamfanya kuwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Yule Aliyetiwa Mafuta. Yesu alikwenda kila mahali akitenda mambo mema. Aliwaponya watu wote ambao Ibilisi alikuwa akiwaumiza na kuwatawala, kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power: God set Jesus apart as the Christ, the Anointed One
decisions.reason: The verb "anoint" is the root of the title Christ, the Anointed One. Kings and priests were anointed with oil; Jesus was anointed with the Spirit at his baptism (Luke 3:22). In Nazareth he read Isaiah 61:1, "the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me", and said it was fulfilled (Luke 4:18-21). Compare 4:27.

decisions.choice: all Judea: the whole land of the Jews, including Galilee
decisions.reason: Here Judea means the whole Jewish homeland, since it began in Galilee, as in Luke 23:5.

decisions.choice: beginning from Galilee: the events began there; the word agrees loosely with the sentence
decisions.reason: The participle does not fit the grammar neatly, like the start of 10:36. The sense is clear: the story began in Galilee.

decisions.choice: Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed him: the subject of what they know is put first
alternatives: Jesus is the one who knows
decisions.reason: Greek often names the person first and then says what is known about him: "you know about Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him".

decisions.choice: oppressed by the devil: held under the devil's power, by sickness and by evil spirits
decisions.reason: The verb means to overpower or dominate. Luke counts both sickness and evil spirits among the devil's works (Luke 13:16).

decisions.choice: God was with him: God's presence and power were at work in Jesus
alternatives: Jesus was only a good man
decisions.reason: Peter speaks first of what his hearers could see; he goes on to call Jesus Lord of all (10:36) and judge of the living and the dead (10:42). Nicodemus says the same of Jesus's signs (John 3:2).

decisions.choice: God poured out the Holy Spirit and power on him, and so made him the Christ, the Anointed One
alternatives: God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power
decisions.reason: Readable explains anointing and links it to the title Christ, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: everyone the devil held in his grip / whom the devil was hurting and controlling
alternatives: all who were oppressed by the devil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the picture of oppression in plainer words.

decisions.choice: after John told people to be baptized
alternatives: after the baptism that John proclaimed
decisions.reason: Readable explains that John called people to be baptized (Luke 3:3).

decisions.choice: le Messie, celui qui a reçu l’onction
decisions.reason: The English Readable glosses the title as "the Anointed One"; "l’Oint" is a rare word for young French readers, so Readable says what it means, keeping the link with "onction".

decisions.choice: alivyomtia mafuta (L, B); Ibilisi
decisions.reason: God anointed Jesus, set him apart as the Christ (meaning decision on anointed): "kumtia mafuta" is the usual Swahili for anointing to an office. The devil is "Ibilisi", the book-wide word. The free "naye" for Jesus takes the span.

source.text: καὶ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.

records.literal_gloss: And we [are] witnesses of all things which he did in both the region of the Jews and Jerusalem; whom also they killed having hanged on a tree.

en.L: And we are witnesses of all things that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; and they killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by hanging [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] on a tree.
en.B: We ourselves saw all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, both in the Jewish countryside and in Jerusalem, and we testify to it. Yet they put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, hanging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a tree.
en.R: We apostles saw everything Jesus did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem, and we tell people about it. But the people of Jerusalem and their leaders killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a wooden cross.

es.L: Y nosotros [somos] testigos de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo, tanto en la región de los judíos como en Jerusalén; y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mataron, colgándolo de un árbol.
es.B: Nosotros mismos vimos todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo en la región de los judíos y en Jerusalén, y damos testimonio de ello. Sin embargo, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mataron colgándolo de un árbol.
es.R: Nosotros, los apóstoles, vimos todo lo que Jesús hizo en la tierra de los judíos y en Jerusalén, y se lo contamos a la gente. Pero la gente de Jerusalén y sus líderes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mataron. Lo clavaron en una cruz de madera.

fr.L: Et nous, [nous sommes] témoins de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait dans le pays des Juifs et à Jérusalem ; {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qu’ils ont même tué en {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pendant au bois.
fr.B: Nous avons vu nous-mêmes tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait dans la campagne juive et à Jérusalem, et nous en rendons témoignage. Pourtant, ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont mis à mort en {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pendant au bois.
fr.R: Nous, les apôtres, nous avons vu tout ce que Jésus a fait dans le pays des Juifs et à Jérusalem, et nous le racontons aux gens. Mais les habitants de Jérusalem et leurs chefs {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont tué. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont cloué sur une croix en bois.

sw.L: Nasi tu mashahidi wa mambo yote aliyoyafanya katika nchi ya Wayahudi na katika Yerusalemu; ambaye pia walimwua kwa kumtundika juu ya mti.
sw.B: Sisi wenyewe tuliona yote aliyoyafanya katika nchi ya Wayahudi na katika Yerusalemu, nasi tunayashuhudia. Hata hivyo walimwua kwa kumtundika juu ya mti.
sw.R: Sisi mitume tuliona kila kitu ambacho Yesu alifanya katika nchi ya Wayahudi na katika Yerusalemu, nasi tunawaambia watu habari hizo. Lakini watu wa Yerusalemu na viongozi wao walimwua. Walimpigilia misumari kwenye msalaba wa mti.

decisions.choice: we are witnesses: the apostles saw these things and tell of them
decisions.reason: A witness in Acts is one who saw and now testifies (1:8, 1:22, 2:32). Those with Peter from Joppa were not among them.

decisions.choice: hanging him on a tree: the words of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law said that anyone hanged on a tree was under God's curse. Peter used the same words before the council (5:30); Paul explains them in Galatians 3:13.

decisions.choice: they killed: the people of Jerusalem and their rulers
decisions.reason: Peter has said the same in 2:23, 3:15 and 5:30. Here the subject is understood from "Jerusalem"; 13:27-28 speaks of those living in Jerusalem and their rulers.

decisions.choice: saw ... and we testify to it / tell people about it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say both sides of being a witness, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: nailed him to a wooden cross
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "hanging on a tree" refers to; Literal and Balanced keep the words of the law.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem and their leaders
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: de un árbol
decisions.reason: As the English "tree": it keeps the wording of Deuteronomy 21:22-23 that Peter echoes (meaning decision m2). Readable says "una cruz de madera", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: en le pendant au bois
decisions.reason: The words echo the law of Deuteronomy 21:22-23 (m2), which French traditionally gives as "pendu au bois"; "au bois" also points to the wooden cross, where "à un arbre" would suggest a living tree.

decisions.choice: kwa kumtundika juu ya mti (L, B); walimpigilia misumari kwenye msalaba wa mti (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Deuteronomy 21:22-23 (meaning decision on hanging him on a tree); Literal and Balanced keep "mti" (tree, wood) so the allusion stays; Readable says what was done, as the English Readable does.

source.text: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι, οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσι τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·

records.literal_gloss: This one the God raised on the third day and gave him visible to become, \v 41 not to all the people but to witnesses those having been chosen beforehand by the God, to us, who ate with and drank with him after the rising of him from [the] dead;

en.L: This one God raised on the third day and granted that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} become visible, \v 41 not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen beforehand by God, to us, who ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rose from [the] dead;
en.B: God raised this same Jesus on the third day and allowed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to appear openly, \v 41 though not to the whole people. He appeared to witnesses whom God had chosen ahead of time, to us. We ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had risen from the dead.
en.R: But on the third day God raised Jesus back to life. God let people see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 41 but not everyone. Only some people saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the ones God had chosen before to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witnesses. We are those people. We ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to life.

es.L: A este lo resucitó Dios al tercer día y concedió que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se hiciera visible, \v 41 no a todo el pueblo, sino a los testigos escogidos de antemano por Dios, a nosotros, que comimos y bebimos con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} después que resucitó de entre [los] muertos;
es.B: Dios resucitó a este mismo Jesús al tercer día y permitió que se dejara ver claramente, \v 41 aunque no por todo el pueblo. Se apareció a testigos que Dios había escogido de antemano, a nosotros. Nosotros comimos y bebimos con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} después que resucitó de entre los muertos.
es.R: Pero al tercer día Dios hizo que Jesús volviera a la vida. Dios dejó que la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} viera, \v 41 pero no todos. Solo algunas personas {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron, las que Dios había escogido antes para ser {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} testigos. Nosotros somos esas personas. Comimos y bebimos con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} después de que volvió a la vida.

fr.L: Celui-là, Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité le troisième jour et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donné de devenir visible, \v 41 non à tout le peuple, mais aux témoins choisis d’avance par Dieu, à nous qui avons mangé et bu avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est ressuscité des morts ;
fr.B: Ce Jésus, Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité le troisième jour et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donné de se montrer ouvertement, \v 41 non pas à tout le peuple, mais aux témoins que Dieu avait choisis d’avance, c’est-à-dire à nous. Nous avons mangé et bu avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est relevé d’entre les morts.
fr.R: Mais le troisième jour, Dieu a ramené Jésus à la vie. Dieu a permis qu’on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voie, \v 41 mais pas tout le monde. Seulement quelques personnes {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu : celles que Dieu avait choisies à l’avance pour être {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} témoins. Ces personnes, c’est nous. Nous avons mangé et bu avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est revenu à la vie.

sw.L: Huyu Mungu alimfufua siku ya tatu, akamjalia aonekane waziwazi, \v 41 si kwa watu wote, bali kwa mashahidi waliochaguliwa tangu awali na Mungu, yaani sisi, tuliokula na kunywa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} baada ya kufufuka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kutoka kwa wafu;
sw.B: Mungu alimfufua Yesu huyu huyu siku ya tatu, akamjalia aonekane waziwazi, \v 41 ingawa si kwa watu wote. Aliwatokea mashahidi ambao Mungu alikuwa amewachagua tangu mwanzo, yaani sisi. Sisi tulikula na kunywa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} baada ya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kufufuka kutoka kwa wafu.
sw.R: Lakini siku ya tatu Mungu alimfufua Yesu. Mungu aliwaruhusu watu wamwone, \v 41 lakini si kila mtu. Ni watu fulani tu waliomwona, wale ambao Mungu alikuwa amewachagua tangu mwanzo kuwa mashahidi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Sisi ndio watu hao. Tulikula na kunywa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} baada ya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kufufuka.

decisions.choice: granted that he become visible: God let the risen Jesus be seen
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses that Jesus was really seen; 10:41 adds that they ate and drank with him (Luke 24:41-43).

decisions.choice: witnesses chosen beforehand by God: God chose who would see the risen Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb means to appoint ahead of time. Jesus chose the apostles (1:2), and God gave them this task (1:8, 1:22).

decisions.choice: ate and drank with him: proof that he had risen bodily
decisions.reason: Luke tells how the risen Jesus ate in front of the disciples (Luke 24:41-43; Acts 1:4).

decisions.choice: all the people: the people of Israel as a whole
decisions.reason: "The people" again means Israel (10:2, 10:42).

decisions.choice: God let people see him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the phrase simply.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: Readable shortens the phrase; the meaning note says who the people are.

source.text: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: and he commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify that this one is the [one] having been appointed by the God judge of living and dead.

en.L: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify solemnly that this is the one appointed by God [as] judge of [the] living and [the] dead.
en.B: He gave us orders to announce this to the people and to declare solemnly that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one God has appointed as judge of the living and of the dead.
en.R: Jesus told us to preach to the people. He told us to tell them clearly that God has chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be the judge of all people, those who are alive and those who have died.

es.L: y nos ordenó proclamar al pueblo y testificar solemnemente que este es el que ha sido designado por Dios [como] juez de vivos y muertos.
es.B: Nos mandó anunciar esto al pueblo y declarar solemnemente que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es aquel a quien Dios ha nombrado juez de los vivos y de los muertos.
es.R: Jesús nos mandó predicar al pueblo. Nos mandó decirles claramente que Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha escogido para ser el juez de todas las personas, de las que están vivas y de las que han muerto.

fr.L: et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a ordonné de prêcher au peuple et d’attester que c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a été désigné par Dieu [comme] juge des vivants et des morts.
fr.B: Il nous a ordonné de l’annoncer au peuple et d’attester solennellement que c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que Dieu a établi juge des vivants et des morts.
fr.R: Jésus nous a dit de prêcher au peuple. Il nous a dit d’expliquer clairement que Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a choisi pour juger tous les gens, ceux qui sont vivants et ceux qui sont morts.

sw.L: {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alituagiza tuwahubiri watu na kushuhudia kwa dhati kwamba huyu ndiye aliyewekwa na Mungu [kuwa] hakimu wa walio hai na wafu.
sw.B: Yeye alituamuru tuwatangazie watu jambo hili na kushuhudia kwa dhati kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye ambaye Mungu amemweka kuwa hakimu wa walio hai na wa wafu.
sw.R: Yesu alituambia tuwahubiri watu. Alituambia tuwaeleze wazi kwamba Mungu amemchagua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa hakimu wa watu wote, walio hai na waliokufa.

decisions.choice: he commanded: the risen Jesus gave the command
decisions.reason: The subject could be God, the subject of 10:40. But the command to the witnesses comes from Jesus after he rose (1:2, 1:8; Luke 24:47-48).

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 10:41; the message then reaches the Gentiles too, as here in Cornelius's house.

decisions.choice: appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead: Jesus will judge all people, at his coming
decisions.reason: Paul says the same in Athens (17:31). "The living and the dead" means everyone who has ever lived (2 Timothy 4:1, 1 Peter 4:5).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, as the meaning note explains, and marks the choice as uncertain.

decisions.choice: the judge of all people, those who are alive and those who have died
alternatives: judge of the living and the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair means.

decisions.choice: hakimu wa walio hai na wafu
decisions.reason: Jesus as the one who will judge all people (meaning decision on judge): "hakimu" is the book-wide word for a judge; "mwamuzi" is kept for the leaders of Israel and the dispute in Acts 7:27.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} (L); Yeye at the start of the sentence (B)
decisions.reason: The free pronouns for Jesus take the span; a pronoun that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital, as the style guide says.

source.text: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: To this one all the prophets bear witness, forgiveness of sins to receive through the name of him everyone the [one] believing in him.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} receives forgiveness of sins through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."
en.B: Every one of the prophets bears witness to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: whoever believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} has their sins forgiven through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."
en.R: All the prophets wrote about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said that God forgives the sins of everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because of who Jesus is and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done."

es.L: Todos los profetas dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: que todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recibe el perdón de los pecados por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre».
es.B: Cada uno de los profetas da testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: quien cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recibe por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre el perdón de sus pecados».
es.R: Todos los profetas escribieron acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Dijeron que Dios perdona los pecados de todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, por quien es Jesús y por lo que ha hecho».

fr.L: À {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tous les prophètes rendent témoignage : quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} reçoit par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom le pardon des péchés. »
fr.B: Tous les prophètes, sans exception, témoignent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} voit ses péchés pardonnés grâce à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. »
fr.R: Tous les prophètes ont parlé de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils ont dit que Dieu pardonne les péchés de tous ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, à cause de ce que Jésus est et de ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait. »

sw.L: Huyu manabii wote wanamshuhudia, kwamba kila amwaminiye hupokea msamaha wa dhambi kupitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}."
sw.B: Manabii wote wanamshuhudia: kila anayemwamini anasamehewa dhambi zake kupitia jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}."
sw.R: Manabii wote waliandika habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Walisema kwamba Mungu humsamehe dhambi kila mtu anayemwamini Yesu, kwa sababu ya jinsi Yesu alivyo na mambo aliyoyafanya."

decisions.choice: all the prophets bear witness: the Scriptures as a whole point to Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter does not quote one text. Jesus taught that the law, the prophets and the psalms speak of him (Luke 24:27, 24:44-47), and Peter said all the prophets announced these days (3:18, 3:24). Isaiah 53:5-6, 53:11 and Jeremiah 31:34 speak of sins taken away.

decisions.choice: through his name: through who he is and what he has done
alternatives: by saying his name as a formula
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person, as in 3:16 and 4:12.

decisions.choice: everyone who believes in him: anyone at all, Jew or Gentile
decisions.reason: "Everyone" is the point of this speech: God has no favorites (10:34). As Peter says it, the Spirit falls on his Gentile hearers (10:44).

decisions.choice: because of who Jesus is and what he has done
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: God forgives the sins
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives.

source.text: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: Still speaking the Peter the words these fell the Spirit the Holy upon all those hearing the word.

en.L: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.
en.B: Peter was still saying these things when the Holy Spirit came down on everyone who was listening to the message.
en.R: Peter was still speaking when the Holy Spirit came on all the people who were listening to the message.

es.L: Todavía hablaba Pedro estas palabras cuando el Espíritu Santo cayó sobre todos los que escuchaban la palabra.
es.B: Pedro todavía estaba diciendo estas cosas cuando el Espíritu Santo descendió sobre todos los que escuchaban el mensaje.
es.R: Pedro todavía estaba hablando cuando el Espíritu Santo vino sobre todas las personas que escuchaban el mensaje.

fr.L: Pierre prononçant encore ces paroles, l’Esprit Saint tomba sur tous ceux qui entendaient la parole.
fr.B: Pierre parlait encore quand l’Esprit Saint descendit sur tous ceux qui écoutaient le message.
fr.R: Pierre parlait encore quand l’Esprit Saint est venu sur tous les gens qui écoutaient son message.

sw.L: Petro alipokuwa bado akisema maneno haya, Roho Mtakatifu aliwaangukia wote waliokuwa wakilisikia neno.
sw.B: Petro alipokuwa bado akisema hayo, Roho Mtakatifu aliwashukia wote waliokuwa wakisikiliza ujumbe huo.
sw.R: Petro alikuwa bado akisema, ndipo Roho Mtakatifu akawajia watu wote waliokuwa wakisikiliza ujumbe huo.

decisions.choice: fell upon: came suddenly and powerfully
decisions.reason: Peter says in 11:15 that the Spirit fell on them as on the apostles at the beginning (2:1-4). It happened before Peter had finished, and before anyone was baptized or had hands laid on them (compare 8:17).

decisions.choice: the word: the message about Jesus that Peter was speaking
decisions.reason: As in 10:36 and 4:4, "the word" is the message of the gospel.

decisions.choice: came down on / came on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a plainer verb; Literal keeps "fell", the word Peter repeats in 11:15.

source.text: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται·

records.literal_gloss: And were amazed the from circumcision believers as many as came with the Peter, that also upon the Gentiles the gift of the Holy Spirit has been poured out;

en.L: And the believers from [the] circumcision who had come with Peter were amazed, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles;
en.B: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on Gentiles too.
en.R: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed. God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift even to people who were not Jews!

es.L: Y quedaron asombrados los creyentes procedentes de [la] circuncisión que habían venido con Pedro, porque el don del Espíritu Santo había sido derramado también sobre los gentiles;
es.B: Los creyentes judíos que habían acompañado a Pedro estaban atónitos, porque el don del Espíritu Santo había sido derramado también sobre los gentiles.
es.R: Los creyentes judíos que habían venido con Pedro quedaron asombrados. ¡Dios había dado el Espíritu Santo como regalo incluso a personas que no eran judías!

fr.L: Et les croyants issus de la circoncision, tous ceux qui étaient venus avec Pierre, furent stupéfaits de ce que le don de l’Esprit Saint avait été répandu aussi sur les nations ;
fr.B: Les croyants juifs qui étaient venus avec Pierre furent stupéfaits de voir que le don de l’Esprit Saint était répandu aussi sur les non-Juifs.
fr.R: Les croyants juifs venus avec Pierre étaient très étonnés. Dieu avait donné l’Esprit Saint en cadeau, même à des gens qui n’étaient pas juifs !

sw.L: Na waaminio wa tohara, wote waliokuja pamoja na Petro, walishangaa, kwa sababu hata juu ya watu wa mataifa kipawa cha Roho Mtakatifu kimemiminwa;
sw.B: Waumini Wayahudi waliokuja pamoja na Petro walishangaa sana kwamba kipawa cha Roho Mtakatifu kilikuwa kimemiminwa hata juu ya watu wa mataifa.
sw.R: Waumini Wayahudi waliokuja pamoja na Petro walishangaa. Mungu alikuwa amewapa Roho Mtakatifu kama zawadi hata watu wasio Wayahudi!

decisions.choice: the believers from the circumcision: Jewish believers
alternatives: a party that insisted on circumcision
decisions.reason: Here the phrase simply means the believers who were Jews by birth, the brothers from Joppa (10:23). In 11:2 a similar phrase names those in Jerusalem who objected.

decisions.choice: poured out: the words of Joel's prophecy
decisions.reason: Peter quoted Joel at Pentecost: God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh (2:17-18, 2:33; Joel 3:1-2 in the Hebrew numbering). Now that includes Gentiles.

decisions.choice: the gift of the Holy Spirit: the gift that is the Spirit himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:38; 11:17 says God gave them the same gift.

decisions.choice: people who were not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift
alternatives: the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver, as the passive implies, and puts the gift as the Spirit himself.

decisions.choice: los gentiles (L, B); personas que no eran judías (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for non-Jews: here the Greek means the people of the nations, not the nations as states. Readable follows the English Readable "people who were not Jews".

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); des gens qui n’étaient pas juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the New Testament. "Les païens" now suggests people without religion, which Cornelius was not; Readable explains the word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: waaminio wa tohara (L); waumini Wayahudi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jewish believers (meaning decision on the believers from the circumcision). Literal keeps the phrase, as Acts 11:2 keeps "wale wa tohara"; Balanced and Readable say who they were.

source.text: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: they were hearing for them speaking in tongues and magnifying the God.

en.L: for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God.
en.B: For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising the greatness of God.
en.R: They knew this because they heard these people speaking in tongues, as the believers did at Pentecost, and praising God for how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

es.L: porque los oían hablar en lenguas y engrandecer a Dios.
es.B: Pues los oían hablar en lenguas y alabar la grandeza de Dios.
es.R: Lo sabían porque oían a esas personas hablar en lenguas, como habían hecho los creyentes en Pentecostés, y alabar a Dios por lo grande que es.

fr.L: car ils les entendaient parler en langues et magnifier Dieu.
fr.B: En effet, ils les entendaient parler en langues et célébrer la grandeur de Dieu.
fr.R: Ils le savaient parce qu’ils entendaient ces gens parler en langues, comme les croyants à la Pentecôte, et louer Dieu pour {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grandeur.

sw.L: kwa maana waliwasikia wakinena kwa lugha na kumtukuza Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa maana waliwasikia wakinena kwa lugha na kuusifu ukuu wa Mungu.
sw.R: Walijua hivyo kwa sababu waliwasikia watu hao wakinena kwa lugha nyingine, kama waumini walivyofanya siku ya Pentekoste, na wakimsifu Mungu kwa ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: speaking in tongues: speech given by the Spirit, as at Pentecost
decisions.reason: At Pentecost the believers spoke in languages that hearers from many nations understood (2:4-11). Peter says these Gentiles received the same gift as the apostles at the beginning (11:15, 11:17), but Luke does not say whether anyone here understood the languages.

decisions.choice: magnifying God: praising God's greatness
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare great, as in Luke 1:46. At Pentecost too the believers spoke of the mighty works of God (2:11).

decisions.choice: as the believers did at Pentecost
decisions.reason: Readable draws the link that Peter himself draws in 11:15.

decisions.choice: wakinena kwa lugha (L, B); wakinena kwa lugha nyingine (R)
decisions.reason: Speech given by the Spirit, as at Pentecost (meaning decision on speaking in tongues). "Lugha" is the word used in Acts 2; Readable adds "nyingine" as Acts 2:4 does and names Pentecost, as the English Readable does.

source.text: τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·

records.literal_gloss: Then answered Peter,

en.L: Then Peter answered,
en.B: Then Peter said,
en.R: Then Peter said,

es.L: Entonces respondió Pedro:
es.B: Entonces Pedro dijo:
es.R: Entonces Pedro dijo:

fr.L: Alors Pierre répondit :
fr.B: Alors Pierre dit :
fr.R: Alors Pierre a dit :

sw.L: Ndipo Petro akajibu,
sw.B: Ndipo Petro akasema,
sw.R: Ndipo Petro akasema,

decisions.choice: answered: responded to what had happened
decisions.reason: No one had asked anything. The verb often means to respond to a situation, here to the Spirit's coming.

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: Since no one asked a question, Balanced and Readable say "said".

source.text: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Not the water is able to forbid anyone, the not to be baptized these, who the Spirit the Holy received as also we?

en.L: "Can anyone withhold the water, so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we also [did]?"
en.B: "Surely no one can refuse the water to keep these people from being baptized. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we did!"
en.R: "These people have received the Holy Spirit, just as we did. So no one can stop them from being baptized with water!"

es.L: «¿Puede alguno negarles el agua para que estos no sean bautizados, ellos que han recibido el Espíritu Santo tal como nosotros también?».
es.B: «Sin duda nadie puede negarles el agua para impedir que estos sean bautizados. ¡Han recibido el Espíritu Santo igual que nosotros!».
es.R: «Estas personas han recibido el Espíritu Santo, igual que nosotros. ¡Así que nadie puede impedir que sean bautizados con agua!».

fr.L: « Quelqu’un peut-il refuser l’eau, pour que ne soient pas baptisés ceux-ci, qui ont reçu l’Esprit Saint tout comme nous ? »
fr.B: « Personne, assurément, ne peut refuser l’eau et empêcher ces gens d’être baptisés. Ils ont reçu l’Esprit Saint tout comme nous ! »
fr.R: « Ces gens ont reçu l’Esprit Saint, comme nous. Alors personne ne peut les empêcher d’être baptisés dans l’eau ! »

sw.L: "Je, mtu yeyote aweza kuyazuia maji, ili hawa wasibatizwe, ambao wamempokea Roho Mtakatifu kama vile sisi pia?"
sw.B: "Hakika hakuna mtu awezaye kuzuia maji ili watu hawa wasibatizwe. Wamempokea Roho Mtakatifu kama sisi!"
sw.R: "Watu hawa wamempokea Roho Mtakatifu kama sisi tulivyompokea. Kwa hiyo hakuna mtu anayeweza kuwazuia wasibatizwe kwa maji!"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no: no one can refuse them baptism
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the question expects "no". Peter recalls this in 11:17: who was he to stand in God's way?

decisions.choice: who have received the Holy Spirit just as we did: God has already accepted them
decisions.reason: Peter reasons from what God has done. In 15:8-9 he says God gave them the Spirit and made no distinction between them and the Jews.

decisions.choice: withhold: forbid, prevent
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 8:36 and 11:17, and of children in Luke 18:16.

decisions.choice: a statement rather than a question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects.

source.text: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: He commanded and them in the name of Jesus Christ to be baptized.

en.L: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: So he gave orders for them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: So Peter told them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Y les mandó que fueran bautizados en el nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Así que dio órdenes de que fueran bautizados en el nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Entonces Pedro les dijo que se bautizaran en el nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

fr.L: Et il ordonna qu’ils soient baptisés au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Il donna donc l’ordre de les baptiser au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Alors Pierre leur a dit de se faire baptiser au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

sw.L: Naye akaamuru wabatizwe katika jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo aliagiza wabatizwe katika jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Petro aliwaambia wabatizwe katika jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: calling on Jesus and coming under his authority
decisions.reason: As in 2:38 and 8:16.

decisions.choice: he commanded them to be baptized: Peter gave the order; others may have baptized them
decisions.reason: The Greek says Peter ordered it, not who did it, as Paul often left baptizing to others (1 Corinthians 1:14-17).

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

source.text: τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.

records.literal_gloss: Then they asked him to remain days some.

en.L: Then they asked him to stay some days.
en.B: Then they asked him to stay on with them for a few days.
en.R: Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few more days.

es.L: Entonces le rogaron que se quedara algunos días.
es.B: Luego le pidieron que se quedara con ellos unos días.
es.R: Después le pidieron a Pedro que se quedara con ellos unos días más.

fr.L: Alors ils lui demandèrent de rester quelques jours.
fr.B: Ils le prièrent alors de demeurer quelques jours avec eux.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils ont demandé à Pierre de rester encore quelques jours avec eux.

sw.L: Ndipo wakamwomba akae siku kadhaa.
sw.B: Kisha wakamwomba akae nao kwa siku chache.
sw.R: Kisha wakamwomba Petro akae nao kwa siku chache zaidi.

decisions.choice: to stay some days: as their guest, eating and lodging in a Gentile house
decisions.reason: Staying with Gentiles is what the believers in Jerusalem criticized: "you went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them" (11:3).
